meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means accept .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means control .

The sun is coming up out of the ground, making this radical dawn . Of course, don't confuse this with dusk! You can do that by thinking that the sun is an optimistic and bright thing, so it tends to come up, not go down. (Also, Japan is the Land of the Rising Sun. I mean come on!)

There is a hat covering the moon and it's holding a knife. Wait, that's no moon. It's a space station! It's the Death Star ! It's pretending to be a moon under that hat. And it's armed! Don't let the Death Star stab your planet to death.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means guest .

Who's that guy wearing Korean clothes? That is a man from Korea , and this is the Korea radical—go figure! He's wearing a samo hat on his head to complete the rest of his hanbok outfit. Alternatively, you can remember this one using the radical components: There are five mouths eating cow at a Korean BBQ. Korea is famous for their delicious BBQ, and you need a lot of people to eat all that beef. At least five people. (Get it? Five people!) That's why this radical is Korea.

Under the ground there's a thread. It traces your lineage . Follow it down through generations of buried relatives to find out your lineage probably involves Genghis Khan or Charlemagne. Feel the thread and the dirt in your hand as you literally trace your lineage.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means nature .

There are people under a canopy on the street forming their own agency . They're banding together right here in the street, making a new government office ! Hints Imagine them putting together papers, talking to politicians, and standing in the street outside the capitol. They demand for this agency to be formed. They are doing all the correct, legal things to do it too.
readingMnemonic: This new agency is just starting to make progress when you hear a low rumble... then a screech. "THIS IS MY STREET. NO NEW AGENCIES ON MY STREET!" Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ) cries as she barrels into everyone. Hints "Whenever you're in a 丁 , you're in my territory," she yells, taking out a few agency members with her fists. "You won't be starting any kind of agency here, not on my watch." And she lights it all on fire.

meaningMnemonic: When you have a guest over, you give them a geoduck because it's worth a huge amount . You're nothing if not a hospitable host. This kanji, weirdly, can also mean picture frame or forehead . Why? Who knows. Just imagine going to a museum and seeing a geoduck in a picture frame, and scratching your forehead in confusion because it's supposedly worth a vast amount of money. Modern art, am I right? Hints Picture a geoduck with a huge amount listed on a price tag attached to it. What amount did you imagine? That's the amount you're basically giving away to your guests.
readingMnemonic: The geoduck you gift to your guest is worth such a lavish amount that it makes them gawk ( がく ). Everyone gawks when they see a geoduck, really — first at how weird it looks, and then at the amount it's worth. Hints Imagine one of your guests gawking in disbelief as you hand them a huge, freshly-caught geoduck worth an ungodly amount of money. Revel in their gawking stare. Feels good, doesn't it?

meaningMnemonic: The moon shines on your roof in the evening and a snake suddenly appears! Wait, that's not a snake, it's your arm , sticking out from under the roof. Hints Arms really look like snakes in the moonlight. Picture it. Your arm is long and shiny, just like a snake.
readingMnemonic: Your arm is exposed to the moon and the outside and you feel a chill. Where are your clothes? Ah, you're n ude, eh ( うで )?! I guess it is pretty common to sleep in the nude, eh? Hints Your arms are nude, eh? That's why they look like snakes, you know. You should be more careful.

meaningMnemonic: Inside this moon is a black hole ... haha just kidding, it's your belly ! It's beautiful and round like the moon and it eats up everything you give it like a black hole. What a good stomach you have! Hints Look down at your perfect belly. It's looking back up at you.
readingMnemonic: If you don't treat your belly with respect, when you look down at it, it'll yell, " F**k ( ふく ) you!" Whoa, looks like someone's got an upset stomach. Hints Forget to eat lunch? Belly grumbles, "F**k you." Call yourself fat and say you need to lose weight? Belly cries, "F**k you!" Be nice to your belly.

meaningMnemonic: The dirt where you just stand and see is a boundary . You don't want to cross the boundary, you just stand there and see over it. As a general rule, you can stand in the dirt and see beyond boundaries, but you don't usually cross them. Hints Imagine a big line in the dirt where you stand and see over into the other side: that's a boundary. The boundary between your home and your neighbor's, the boundary between cities or countries… Some you can cross, and some you can't.
readingMnemonic: The boundary you're looking at now is the Kyo to ( きょう ) boundary. Kyoto is one of the most famous places in Japan, so you can imagine its boundary is really clear and marked by all kinds of boundary signs that say KYOTO. Hints Picture yourself outside of Kyoto. Picture the boundary between you and Kyoto. Now hop over it!

meaningMnemonic: Fire in nature will burn down everything in its path. In nature, there are no firefighters to contain the flames, so the blaze will burn until nothing's left. Hints Feel the fire all around you as it burns. You're out in nature — the middle of a forest fire. Hear the woods crackle as they burn up around you.
readingMnemonic: What is the worst thing that could burn in this fire? Your nen doroid ( ねん ) collection. You've spent a lot of time and money collecting all these cool and rare and unique nendoroids and now they've all burned in the fire. Hints Cry your eyes out as you smell the burning plastic of your nendoroids. Worst. Day. Ever.

meaningMnemonic: You use your fingers at dawn to carry many things. You have to carry yourself out of bed. You have to carry your backpack or purse or laptop bag to school or work. Your fingers have to carry a lot of weight around at dawn. Hints Think about your morning routine. You carry yourself into the bathroom and carry a toothbrush into your mouth. You carry your coat and bag out the door.
readingMnemonic: Once you're carry ing everything, and the dawn sun is shining bright, you start getting tan ( たん ). Especially those fingers you're using to carry things. Hints Picture yourself carrying a coat and a bag, walking through the rice fields to work, with the hot, dawn sun shining down, making your fingers get tanner and tanner.

meaningMnemonic: If a spirit blesses your older brother it's time to celebrate ! This isn't something that happens every day to everyone's older brother. Yours is very good and very lucky. So celebrate with him! Hints Imagine what celebrating would be like. Imagine an older brother too, if you don't actually have one.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, the two of you celebrate d too much, and you went a little crazy. The spirit grabbed your brother and shook ( しゅく ) him. Shook him so hard his head popped off. Hints Never celebrate too hard. Otherwise you'll always have to think about the time a celebration spirit shook your brother till his head fell off.

meaningMnemonic: The American flag is the reason you need to deliver this package. The flag is inside the package, and you need to deliver it to the president. He lost his old flag, so now it’s up to you to deliver this new one to him. What more of a reason do you need? Hints You need to deliver this flag to the president. Imagine yourself running as fast as you can while carrying the parcel in order to get it to him. Your lungs are tired and your legs burn, but you must deliver the flag as soon as possible!
readingMnemonic: To deliver this flag is something you just have to do ( とど ). Need to do. Want to do. There is no one else to do it. This is something only you are equipped to do. Hints The world depends on you to do this delivery. If you fail, the United States will be ruined. You have to do it! Deliver that flag now! Run! Run!

meaningMnemonic: You take your scooter to Korea and everything is different ! Hints Imagine scooting down a street in Korea and seeing how different literally every single thing is compared to what you're used to in Japan.
readingMnemonic: What's also different is that there's a weird tiger bouncing on its tail alongside you yelling that its name is Tigger ( ちが ). You didn't know Tigger was living in Korea these days. That's definitely different. Hints Tigger is different in Korea too. For one, he's a white tiger now, and he's, like, really aggressive. Wait, was he always like that?

meaningMnemonic: When a sheep tries its hoof at construction , it gains distinction . Now that is something that really sets a sheep apart! After all, have you ever seen a sheep working in construction? Hints Note that the sheep has to sweep its tail to one side so that it doesn't get in the way of all the construction tools. That's why it looks a little different here. Imagine a sheep in a hard hat, with its tail on one side, getting down to some construction. How very distinctive.
readingMnemonic: The extra distinction of this sheep is that its really skilled with a saw ( さ ). That's why it's so good at construction. Hints Imagine the sheep holding the saw in its hooves. It isn't easy to grip a saw with hooves, but this is no ordinary sheep.

meaningMnemonic: There’s a flag under the blackjack table that you can kick in order to expand the table. Sometimes you only have a few people playing blackjack so you don’t need to kick the flag at all, and sometimes  there are many people playing blackjack so you need to kick the flag many times in order to expand it to a proper size. Hints Imagine yourself kicking this flag to see the blackjack table expand. Feel your foot kicking the flag. You’ve kicked it so many times that your leg is sore, but you need to expand the table some more so you keep kicking it. Imagine the blackjack table making that sound Mario makes whenever he gets a mushroom and expands in size.
readingMnemonic: The blackjack table does have a limit though of how many times it will expand , and that limit is ten ( てん ). You can only kick the flag to get the table to expand ten times. Hints Imagine yourself kicking the flag ten times. Count it off in your head and imagine each instance up to ten. Any more kicks after ten don’t cause the table to do anything, but it does cause your leg to get sore.

meaningMnemonic: You're about to enter a roof that has your number on it so you can face the judge . You've been sitting here for what feels like hours, waiting for your number to come up. Finally the time has come—the judge will see you now. Hints Picture the judge sitting under the roof. Your number is sitting on his big desk, next to the gavel.
readingMnemonic: The judge is not happy with you. He tells you to come closer and when you do, he takes his gavel and hits you in the shin s ( しん ). Ouch! Hints You try to ask the judge what his ruling is, but he just hits you on the shins again!

meaningMnemonic: Behind the flag lies a mask —yet another layer of secrecy. You’re standing in front of a crowd, giving a rousing speech. Hiding your face is the flag of your country, and behind that flag you’re also wearing a mask, just in case the flag falls down. The extra layer of secrecy is just to be safe. Hints These layers are meant to protect you. We all have layers we hide behind sometimes, you know? You can't be totally transparent with everyone.
readingMnemonic: Someone jumps up on stage and starts peeling off your layer s! You stand there, first goes the flag, then the mask, then ... your sou l ( そう ) is laid bare. No, literally. You don't have a body, your soul was under that mask. And now it's floating there for all to see. Hints Everyone in the crowd is completely silent, staring at your soul, with all of its layers peeled off.

meaningMnemonic: The lineage radical and the lineage kanji are the same. Sometimes this kanji can also mean system . I guess a lineage is a kind of system, if you think about it. Hints Basically, think of 系 as linking things that belong together in some kind of group. Lineages, solar systems, genres, styles… Anything along those lines .
readingMnemonic: You trace your lineage back through your whole family system and realize every single relative loved ca ke ( けい ). Most of them were cake bakers too. Hints You come from a lineage of cake makers and cake eaters. No wonder you love cake so much. (And if you hate cake, no wonder your family doesn't like you.)

meaningMnemonic: If you use your spirit to see something, it means you really look at it. You're not just seeing something passively with your eyes, you're actually looking at it with your whole spirit. Hints Imagine using your whole spirit to look at something. Like, you feel your spirit flowing out from your eyes and enveloping whatever you're looking at. It's kind of trippy. When's the last time you really looked at something like that? Try it now.
readingMnemonic: The first thing you want to look at like this is a shee p ( し ). You've seen a lot of sheep, but you've never really looked at them closely, so your image of them is kind of… woolly. Hints Look at a picture of a sheep now. Really look at it with all your spirit. Bet you start noticing some things you'd never seen before, right?

meaningMnemonic: The king is showing his people how to put a net around a weird zombie by walking around it in a loop . It's a weird zombie because it has the ground on top of its head instead of dirt. Hints Watch as the king loops the net around and around and around the zombie, keeping it completely pinned down.
readingMnemonic: The king also explains that this loop technique was used by Genghis Khan ( かん ) when he was conquering cities. He'd loop around the entire place with a net and trap them. Hints Picture Genghis Khan looping around and around just like the king is looping around and around this zombie.

meaningMnemonic: In an attempt to control your clothes , you manufacture a mind control device. This mind control device will allow you to control the mind of your clothes and all that they do. You just need to manufacture it. Hints Imagine being able to control your clothes with your mind. What would you have them do? Imagine what you would do with your clothes if you could manufacture something to control them and move them around at will with your mind.
readingMnemonic: You manufacture these clothes to control your sa ber ( せい ). It's hard to manufacture, you have to do a lot of work, but you manage to make your clothes control your saber. Now you don't need to rely on your hands! Hints Now you're trying to manufacture a machine that will make sabers and clothes you can use to control them. Soon you'll have a manufactured army of saber-controlling clothes!

meaningMnemonic: On this scooter , there's an angel with a drop of sweat coming off of it, because it forgot to mention something to you! It seems like it's something important too, since they're sweating so much. Hints The angel just visited you, but it forgot to mention something important (probably life-threatening, it's an angel after all), and now you see it scooting at top speeds toward you.
readingMnemonic: "I forgot to mention , you have to study nin jutsu ( じゅつ )!" the angel yells. But it's too late, there are ninjas jumping out of the bushes around you and taking you hostage. Hints The angel really should have mentioned ninjutsu earlier. Then maybe you would have gone straight to a dojo to learn instead of falling into a ninjutsu trap yourself. The angel definitely failed its mission.

meaningMnemonic: On the ground there's a ceremony where everyone keeps stop ping. This stopping ceremony is being performed by the military . They'll march one direction, then stop and turn, then march another direction, then stop again. Hints The military really seems to have a thing for stopping a lot during their ceremonies.
readingMnemonic: You look closer at the people in the military and realize that every time they stop they take a drink of boo ze ( ぶ )! Hints This is a ceremony for celebrating the military so I guess they can drink as much booze as they want, but this seems very strange to you.

meaningMnemonic: There is a lantern on top of a knife in the dirt . You walk up to take the knife and lantern when you realize it's just a model . It all looked real from far away, but now that you're up close you can see none of it is real. Hints Why would anyone make a model that looks like a lantern and a knife sticking into the ground?
readingMnemonic: You touch the model and see that it's made of ca ke ( けい )! Someone really into lanterns and knives must have been given this model cake as a birthday present! Though they left it out here so they probably didn't like it. Hints Haven't you seen any of those crazy cakes modeled after things like movies, towns, giants hams, and purses? They're all the rage. Next time you make a cake try to make it look like a model lantern and knife with fake cake dirt and everything.

meaningMnemonic: You have an animal for a husband with horns that are narrow . This animal husband of yours is a goat. A goat with narrow horns. Why is this animal your husband? You’re weird, that’s why. Hints Imagine yourself married to this animal husband with horns that are narrow. It’s a strange marriage. Listen to the goat making its goat noises as it clomps around your home. Now hug your goat husband and feel its soft fluffy coat against your skin.
readingMnemonic: I’m not even going to get into the sema ntics ( せま ) of how this weird relationship of yours works. Nope, this reading explanation is on the straight and narrow . Need to know basis. Classified. All that junk. There will be no discussion of the semantics between you and your goat lover. Hints But that doesn’t mean you can’t imagine the semantics. The finer points of the relationship. Go ahead, imagine all the weird stuff that comes with the territory for having a goat as a husband. Use all that weird stuff to remember this kanji and its reading. Want an example? Just imagine the goat doing dishes! Goats don’t have hands! Hahahahaha!!

meaningMnemonic: When a leader wants to work together , it means they want what you have to offer . Congrats! Now you can accompany them everywhere and offer them hot towels and bottled water, or whatever it is you do… Hints Picture handing things to your leader as you accompany them somewhere. You're happy to do this, but you know you have so much more to offer than a hot towel and a pretty face. When will they see what you really have to offer?!
readingMnemonic: Once a year, the leader will offer you a vacation in きょう と . It's an all-expenses-paid trip! The catch is that you have to accompany your leader to きょうと … Hints Picture you and the leader enjoying some matcha together under the cherry blossoms in きょうと . Yeah, this was definitely worth it. So glad you took them up on their offer and accompanied them.

meaningMnemonic: On your bamboo roof is a bear . It is pulling the bamboo off, because it wants to use it to make a long pipe . Hints Bamboo is great for pipes, and the only place for the bear to get it is your roof. So, that's why it's there.
readingMnemonic: The pipe will be for Genghis Khan ( かん ), who would like some pipes for his house. Hints Watch the bear take away your bamboo. Follow it to Genghis Khan's house. There, the bear installs the pipe in Genghis Khan's bathroom.

meaningMnemonic: You have a cross for a drunkard 's car , to place on its dashboard. Drunkards should not drive, and when you put on a cross, it prevents the car from starting! Hints Imagine the power that starts emanating from the cross once it’s placed on the car, it can’t move even an inch. Nope, it's not going anywhere until its owner sobers up.
readingMnemonic: You have a lot of crosses to place on drunkard cars, so you get your cy borg ( さい ) to do it for you. The cyborg doesn't need sleep, so it can patrol the streets 24/7 for the sake of public safety. What a saintly cyborg. Hints Picture your cyborg, approaching a drunkard's car to place a cross on it. You see it open a big compartment on its chest, and it's filled with crosses.

meaningMnemonic: You have to use two axe s to open these shellfish . That seems like overkill, but it is necessary. These particular shellfish are of very high quality meaning they won't open so easily. Hints Imagine the highest quality shellfish you've ever seen. They're hard, smooth, and basically impenetrable.
readingMnemonic: You finally get all of the shellfish open and you're admiring their quality , when your shih tzu ( しつ ) jumps up on the table and gobbles them down. NO! You try to chase after the little dog, but it's too late. They're gone. Hints I guess your shih tzu knows good quality shellfish too. :(

meaningMnemonic: When dawn reaches this village it increases in quantity . That's right. Every morning the amount of people or animals living here goes up by at least one. Hints Picture dawn, the sun rising, the birds chirping, and the screams of a new born baby rise in the village. Or Maybe it's a new sheep! Or a new hat that someone just finished making.
readingMnemonic: Today's dawn has brought with it an increase in the quantity of row ( りょう ) boats! Aww, aren't they cute? Look at all of the new row boats lined up together. They all have their own sets of oars too. Hints When every dawn brings a new amount of people, those new people are going to need that same amount of row boats.

meaningMnemonic: A sudden aversion to shellfish makes you anti -shellfish, so you sell off every shellfish in sight. Hints If you're serious about being anti-shellfish then you should sell all the ones you have.
readingMnemonic: You're going to sell all of our shellfish to Han ( はん ) Solo. He isn't anti-shellfish like you, and he knows how to turn a profit too! Hints Picture yourself selling all of your shellfish to Han Solo. You stand there with your arms crossed, and Han just shakes his head at you and continues to toss them onto his spaceship.

meaningMnemonic: Take your leather and change it into a pair of shoes . (Most shoes were made out of leather in the old days, you know.) Hints You start with a sheet of leather. Now imagine yourself going through the process of changing it into shoes. Smell the leather, and feel it too. Maybe rub your shoes right now, pretending they're made of leather. Mmm, that's nice.
readingMnemonic: Most shoes aren’t made from leather anymore, but you know who still wears leather shoes? Old coots ( くつ ). The coots are so old that all the shoes they had growing up were made of leather, so they refuse to wear anything else now. Crazy old coots. Hints Imagine these old coots busting into a modern shoe store and kicking over all the display stands and setting everything on fire because they hate non-leather shoes so, so much. Hear the old coots screaming and babbling nonsense as they destroy the shoe store.

meaningMnemonic: The door leading to the moon can be broken down with one’s shoulder . It’s not a very sturdy door to the moon, so it’s quite easy to drop your shoulder and ram it open. Hints Picture yourself smashing through this door using your shoulder and seeing the moon on the other side. Hear the splintering of wood as your shoulder crashes through the door and feel the impact with your body.
readingMnemonic: "Wow, your shoulder is just like my cata pult ( かた )!" you hear someone shout. As you turn you're just in time to see a man catapulting through his own moon door! Hints Now the weird man is inspecting your shoulder really closely and he keeps muttering "catapult powers" under his breath. It's very unsettling, but he's kind of right. A shoulder works just like the mechanism that winds up a catapult.

meaningMnemonic: Every husband you see sets a new standard . It seems like husbands are just getting better and better these days, and whenever you see one the standard has gone up again. Hints Imagine what you see these standard-setting husbands doing. Maybe you see one listening intently to his partner's tedious story. Another lays his coat over a puddle for some lady to walk across. Wow, you see the husband standard going up everywhere.
readingMnemonic: A good husband knows that a high standard is the key ( き )… to his beloved's heart and to a happy marriage. The second he lets his standards slip, he knows the marriage is in trouble. Maintaining a high standard is definitely the key. Hints You can even imagine the sound of a key in a lock every time you see a husband setting a high standard. Like as soon as that one guy put his coat down over that puddle, you heard a key click and a heart open up. *click* And when some random husband politely opened a door for you? *click*

meaningMnemonic: You're stuck in a tree after using the evacuation slide to jump out of your jet — a stunt you pulled after hearing your stock s and share s had taken a dive in the market. Hints Imagine lying battered and bruised in the upper boughs of this tree and thinking about all your worthless stocks and shares. Hopefully you had fun jumping out of your private jet, 'cause you can't afford to ride in it anymore.
readingMnemonic: Your stock s and share s fell so hard that they probably went " KABOO M ( かぶ )!" when they hit rock bottom. Hints Imagine watching a real-time graph of your stock portfolio as its value plummets. The line dives toward the x-axis, and then… KABOOM! Not a cent of value left. Oh well… At least you had fun shouting "KABOOM" as your stocks crashed.

meaningMnemonic: If, at a certain angle , you approach an insect , you’ll be able to touch it without it noticing. Most of the time, insects will run away from you when you try and touch them, but if you do so from the right angle, the insect will have no idea. Hints Imagine yourself approaching this insect from a sneaky and stealthy angle. Now touch it. What does it feel like? Smooth? Hard? Fuzzy? Feel the insect in your mind as you touch it.
readingMnemonic: Uh oh, looks like this particular insect is a lightning bug so when you touch it you get a shock ( しょく ). Did you know that lightning bugs contain bazillions of volts inside them? Well they do, and if you touch one, you get a shock. A very big shock. Hints Feel this electrical shock to your system as you touch the lightning bug. This discourages you from ever touching another insect again. You don’t enjoy the shock.

meaningMnemonic: What does a car and the Death Star have in common? They're both used to transport people and things. Hints Imagine stuffing a bunch of Stormtroopers in your car so you can transport them across the country. Well the Death Star can transport even more Stormtroopers, faster, and through space!
readingMnemonic: Right now you and the Death Star are transport ing yu rts ( ゆ ). They're the universe's #1 best transportable homes! Hints It's easy to transport a yurt even without a car or the Death Star.

meaningMnemonic: You approach the Moon in a helicopter and see a woman there on the surface, touching her waist . She's posing with one hand on her waist, like she's Sailor Moon or something. I guess that would explain what she's doing here on the Moon! Hints Imagine flying your helicopter closer to the woman. Even as you touch down she never takes her hand off her waist. You get closer and try to see why she's touching her waist like that.
readingMnemonic: Once you get close, you see that her waist looks weird and… puffy? You realize she's stuffed some 子 shee p ( こし ) under her skirt's waistband to line her waist with them. Guess it's cold up here on the moon, so the 子 sheep keep her waist warm. And they had to be 子 sheep, otherwise they wouldn't be small enough to fit under her clothes. Hints Imagine how warm your waist would be if you stuffed a bunch of 子 sheep into your waistband. Just don't let anyone see you do it. Pretty sure that's animal cruelty…

meaningMnemonic: Above mention s are above mentioned . Look above to see where I mentioned it, okay? Note that 上述 is a word commonly used in formal writing such as reports, academic papers, or business documents.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 上述の理由から、私は今回のプロジェクトには参加しないことに決めました。
sentences.english: For the reasons mentioned above, I have decided not to participate in this project.

sentences.japanese: 上述の問題を解決するために、私たちが考えた新しいプランを下記に示します。
sentences.english: To solve the aforementioned problem, we present below the new plan that we have come up with.

sentences.japanese: 上述のように、雇用者、従業員のどちらも、いついかなる理由においても契約を終了することができる。
sentences.english: As stated above, both employees and employers can terminate an employment contract at any time for any reason.

meaningMnemonic: The year amount is the annual amount .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 月額よりも年額の方がお得ですよ。
sentences.english: The annual fee is a better deal than the monthly fee.

sentences.japanese: 固定資産税の年額を見ると、その高さにビックリしてしまいます。
sentences.english: When I look at the amount of annual property tax, I am surprised at how expensive it is.

sentences.japanese: 前回のサービスも良かったとは思いますが、今回の新サービスはもっとよくなったと思うんです。それでいて、会員費は変わらず年額80ドルのままなんですよ。
sentences.english: I think the previous service was good, but I think this new service is even better. What's more, the membership fee is still only eighty dollars a year.

meaningMnemonic: The angle of the touch is important with an antenna . Think about antennae. An ant's antennae wiggle around and move in different angles, touching things, to understand the world around them. Imagine their tiny bug antennae touching your arm to figure out who you are. Note that 触角 refers to the antennae of insects, crustaceans, and certain other arthropods, rather than to TV or radio antennas.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. しょく goes to しょっ .

sentences.japanese: アリの触角も美しいが、ちょうちょうの触角の方が一層美しい。
sentences.english: Ants antennae are beautiful, but butterfly antennae are even more beautiful.

sentences.japanese: 虫の触角は触覚だけでなく、臭覚の機能も備えている。
sentences.english: The antennae of insects serve not only as touch sensors but also possess olfactory functions.

sentences.japanese: 蝸牛の触角の先端に目があるなんて知りませんでした！
sentences.english: I didn’t know snail’s eyes are on the tips of their antennae!

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same, so this means arm . While 腕 fundamentally refers to the appendages most of us have dangling from our shoulders, it can also be used figuratively to talk about someone's ability or skill in something, like ギターの腕を上げる (to improve at guitar) or 料理の腕をアピールする (show off one's cooking skills).
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

meaningMnemonic: You hope your efforts will bear fruit , but… will they really ? It remains to be seen. 果たして is a word used to express skepticism or uncertainty about an outcome. For example, you might hear a soccer announcer say 果たしてゴールできるのか？ (will they indeed be able to score?) as a player runs down the field, or an anime character say 果たしてそうなのかな？ (I wonder if that's really the case?) when they're doubting something they've been told. It sounds a bit dramatic and theatrical, so you'll run into it more in entertainment media than in casual conversation. In some cases, it can also mean as was expected , as in 果たして失敗した (as expected, they failed), but this meaning is mostly limited to either older or quite literary writing.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you don't really believe someone, you say, " Hah ( は )! Nice try, but you're not fooling anyone." As was expected , you saw right through their lies. Hah!

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. It's also an intransitive verb, meaning the action happens on its own, you don't do it. meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means carry so the verb vocab version is to carry . meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. meaningMnemonic: The kanji is distinction , and the verb version here means… a million things. Let's just focus on a few common meanings. Things with distinction tend to stick out from the others. They tend to shine , you know? And if you imagine shining a beam of light on something, that light tends to project or to extend outward . It sticks out, shines on something, then makes that thing more distinct too. That's why you can say 光が差す (light shines), かげが差す (a shadow is cast), 指差す (to point at), or even カサを差す (to open and raise an umbrella). Basically, 差す usually has to do with causing something to appear , either by shining or projecting outward.
readingMnemonic: The reading of the kanji is actually the same as the reading for this word, making things easy (both on'yomi and kun'yomi are さ ).

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means stab so the verb vocab version must also be to stab . Wondering how it's different from 刺す ? 突く refers to the act of pushing or pressing something with a tip of an object, often done forcefully and swiftly. So when you use 突く as in "to stab," your focus is on the forcefulness of the action. On the other hand, 刺す focuses more on the actual act of piercing into something or someone with a sharp thing. This is why 突く can be be translated many ways, like to poke , to jab , and many more.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means touch so the verb vocab version is to touch something . 触る is used when someone does the touching. It's not used to describe objects touching each other. Note that 触る can be used with either the particle に or を , like 手に触る or 手を触る (to touch a hand). Using に simply marks the location you touch, while using を highlights your action of touching that specific area or object. So the former is intransitive and the latter is transitive, though there's some debate about that.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You only like to touch things that are sour ( さわ ). Lemons, limes, grapefruits, you name it. There's something about sour things that just makes you want to touch them.

meaningMnemonic: If 伝統 is "tradition," then adding a 的 ( -al ) to it would make it traditional .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: Japan has a lot of traditional culture.

sentences.english: This festival is a traditional event, but it now incorporates a modern essence as well.

sentences.english: Kimono are Japan’s traditional attire, and fundoshi are the traditional Japanese underwear for men.

meaningMnemonic: You want to transport something by send ing it? Well, that's transportation .

sentences.english: Wait, you shipped whisky all the way from Japan in a container!?

sentences.english: Please tell me the transportation cost.

sentences.japanese: ダリンはトラックで新鮮なフグを大量に輸送した。
sentences.english: Darin transported a large number of fresh blowfishes by truck.

meaningMnemonic: Trace something back through its lineage to determine what type of thing it is. 〜系 is a suffix you can attach casually to a word to classify it as a genre or group, like 理系 (science-oriented fields), おしゃれ系 (trendy or stylish people), or 日系 (people of Japanese lineage ).
readingMnemonic: This is the same reading you learned with the kanji, so you should be good to go.

sentences.english: ecosystem

sentences.japanese: 神経系
sentences.english: nervous system

sentences.japanese: きれい系
sentences.english: elegant type

sentences.japanese: 出会い系
sentences.english: apps and websites for dating (as a category)

sentences.japanese: 肉食系
sentences.english: proactive or assertive person (e.g. in dating), "carnivore type"

sentences.japanese: 私の兄はガテン系の陽キャだが、顔は小動物系なのでちょっと可愛い。
sentences.english: My brother is an outgoing, blue-collar guy, but he has such a small-animal face that he's actually kind of adorable.

sentences.english: Mr. Kawamura is a typical corporate person.

sentences.japanese: 典型的なハリウッド映画って感じだったね。

sentences.japanese: それは日本語学習者が犯す典型的な間違いだね。

sentences.english: What are the advantages of small businesses expanding overseas?

sentences.japanese: このエアバッグは車が衝突してもすぐには展開しないので危険なんです。
sentences.english: This air bag is dangerous because it doesn’t deploy right away when the car crashes.

meaningMnemonic: These view s that have merit ( 価値 ) are your values .

sentences.english: I think it’s quite important to share similar values with your spouse.

meaningMnemonic: Automatic ( 自動 ) sell sell machine . The machine sells things by itself, basically. This is a vending machine . There is a shorter version of this, but good to learn the long one first :)

meaningMnemonic: You know about 大統領 ( president ), right? Well, this is the vice version of the president, aka the vice president .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know the word 大統領 first, though.

sentences.japanese: あのがっしりした広い肩の男が、この国の副大統領です。
sentences.english: That guy with broad shoulders is the vice president of this country.

sentences.japanese: 副大統領は大統領にあいさつしたが、完全に無視された。
sentences.english: The vice president greeted the president, but the president completely ignored him.

sentences.japanese: やってみるべきだと思うけど。大統領は無理でも、副大統領ぐらいなら狙えるんじゃない？
sentences.english: I think you should give it a try though. It may not be possible to become the president, but you could try going for vice president.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 腰 refers to the waist area around the top part of the hip bone — the part that sticks out when you put your hands on your hips. It includes the sides and the back as well, which is why this can also mean lower back .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.
